biography: Jamie Hopkins, a name now synonymous with audacious overtakes and the roar of a Ginetta engine, hails from the unassuming town of Market Rasen. Unlike many who dream of racing from childhood, Jamie stumbled into the sport almost by accident. As a teenager working at a local garage, a customer couldn't pay his bill and offered a clapped-out Ginetta G40 as payment. Jamie, initially hesitant, was soon hooked. The raw, visceral experience ignited a passion he never knew he possessed. He started competing in local club races, quickly outgrowing the amateur scene with his raw talent and fearless driving. A defining moment came at Brands Hatch in 2018; starting from the back of the grid due to a qualifying mishap, Jamie carved his way through the field, executing a daring last-corner move to snatch victory. This audacious display caught the eye of the factory Ginetta team, who signed him shortly after. Now, at 28, Jamie is considered to be entering his peak years, hungry for championship glory and determined to make his mark on the sport. The red hair and flashy persona are now as recognisable as the Ginetta he pilots.
drivingStyle: Jamie's driving style is best described as aggressive and opportunistic. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and willingness to take risks, often pushing his car to the absolute limit. While not always the smoothest driver, Jamie possesses incredible car control and an innate ability to find grip where others can't. He's a master of the undercut, using his raw speed to gain track position during pit stops. Tire management isn't his strongest suit, often sacrificing longevity for outright pace, but he compensates with a relentless attacking style that keeps his rivals on their toes. He thrives under pressure, often producing his best results when the stakes are highest.

rivalries.reason: A clash of egos and contrasting styles; Rossi, the methodical and calculated Italian, views Jamie's flamboyant approach as reckless and disrespectful. On track, this has led to several close calls and heated exchanges.

Berg is the polar opposite of Hopkins, a quiet, calculating driver who lets his driving do the talking. Jamie considers Berg to be an 'overrated snooze fest', while Berg probably doesn't even know Jamie exists.

Their rivalry sparked after a controversial incident at Silverstone where Jamie punted Davies off the track while battling for the lead. Davies has vowed revenge, leading to some incredibly tense on-track battles.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of racing socks, even though they're falling apart.
Listens to heavy metal music at deafening volumes right before a race to 'get the blood pumping'.
Has a pre-race ritual of polishing his helmet visor with a specific brand of glass cleaner, believing it improves his vision.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about being polite, it's about being the fastest. If that means ruffling a few feathers, so be it."
careerHighlight: Winning the Ginetta Supercup Championship in 2022 after a season-long battle with veteran racer Mark Thompson. Hopkins secured the title with a dominant victory in the final race at Donington Park, silencing his doubters and proving his championship credentials.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the 24 Hours of Spa in 2023, costing his team a potential victory. The incident, caused by a momentary lapse in concentration, haunted him for months afterwards.
